pages.name: Overview: Variants of the Path of Night

text.content:
The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} claim the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.n1ghtP4thOfN1ght]{Path of Night} as their own, taught in earlier forms far back into antiquity. This entry supplements the base Path of Night entry (see the paths-of-enlightenment compendium) with several named, related variant forms taught among the clan and the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}'s Abyss mystics. Each variant uses the same Hierarchy of Sins framework as the standard Path of Night (sometimes called the "Hot Path") but reinterprets it, or in some cases substitutes different Virtues, per the notes on each page that follows.

Storytellers may permit further player-proposed variations at their discretion, so long as no variation ever makes existence easier for the vampire following it.

Do not duplicate the base Path of Night write-up here — these pages are cross-referenced supplements describing how each named variant diverges from it.

The Cold Path relies on Conviction and Self-Control, rather than Conviction and Instinct as the standard @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.n1ghtP4thOfN1ght]{Path of Night} does. It shares the same Hierarchy of Sins as the standard Path, but interprets each sin differently. For example, a Cold Path follower rejects impassioned or premeditated killing not because it is insufficiently controlled, but because it distracts from contemplating deeper mysteries.

Virtues used: Conviction, Self-Control.

MET: Track this variant as the base Path of Night, substituting Self-Control Virtue Traits for Instinct Virtue Traits where the base Path calls for Instinct.

Favored by many Abyss mystics, the Allied Path replaces the individual's role in the Hierarchy of Sins with the role of the clan as a whole. Level 7 sin is "Asking aid of a vampire of another clan." Level 9 sin is "Acting in the interests of another clan." This variant may use either Self-Control or Instinct, depending on the individual vampire's inclination toward frenzy.

Virtues used: Conviction, and either Self-Control or Instinct (chosen at adoption).

MET: Track as the base @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.n1ghtP4thOfN1ght]{Path of Night}, but reassign sin levels 7 and 9 as above; all other levels follow the base Hierarchy of Sins.

The Lightless Path focuses on darkness as the quintessential @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} condition. Level 10 sin is relying on sight. Level 9 sin is allowing light to strike oneself. Level 8 sin is depredations conducted in the light (killing or wreaking havoc while illuminated). This variant uses Self-Control. The most experienced practitioners of the Lightless Path blind themselves and rely on senses other than sight.

Virtues used: Conviction, Self-Control.

MET: Track as the base @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.n1ghtP4thOfN1ght]{Path of Night}, but reassign sin levels 8-10 as above; all other levels follow the base Hierarchy of Sins.

One of the oldest surviving variants, the Righteous Path was more popular when the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} believed themselves agents of a divine will; Cardinal Monçada's destruction spurred widespread abandonment of this variant. It replaces the individual with all vampires who believe in their divine purpose — accepting the superiority of a fellow Righteous Path practitioner (or a devout follower of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.db3Fhvpv32rhN3Mm]{Path of Caine} or @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.exke2riW9D0htoUu]{Path of Cathari}) is not sinful. The practitioner sins by killing in a way that does not strike fear into sinners' hearts. This variant generally uses Self-Control, though some "fearful angels" packs use Instinct.

Virtues used: Conviction, and typically Self-Control (some packs use Instinct instead).

MET: Track as the base @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.n1ghtP4thOfN1ght]{Path of Night}; reinterpret the standard Hierarchy of Sins per the theological framing above, with the Storyteller adjudicating specific incidents.
